subject: Status page notice: intermittent streaming segment drops impacting completions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novum.ai>, Ava Roy <ava.roy@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Status page notice: intermittent streaming segment drops impacting completions

Hi Samir / Ava,

I wanted to alert you that we're seeing an intermittent issue in our hosted inference service that is causing streaming responses to drop mid-completion for a subset of requests (clients see truncated completions or missing final chunks). The incident is visible on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261230-5.

Impact: a small percentage (~0.4%) of streaming requests across US regions may deliver incomplete payloads. We've observed this primarily on long-running completion streams (>2k tokens) and certain model variants.

What we're doing now: our SRE and runtime teams have opened an incident bridge and are triaging kernel scheduling and KV cache eviction patterns. We have a temporary mitigation plan in place (shortening max segment windows and forcing a light-prefetch on cold sessions) which we expect to push within the hour.

Action for you: if you can, please forward examples (request-id or trace id) of truncated responses — that will help us correlate logs faster. Example header to include: x-redwood-trace-id: RWD-XXXXXXXX.

Next update: I'll post an ETA/update in two hours or sooner. Apologies for the disruption — I know this impacts production behavior and we'll prioritize stabilization.

Attachments: runbook_v1.pdf (incident playbook excerpt)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir@novum.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:28:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Status page notice: intermittent streaming segment drops impacting completions

Thanks Mina — we saw a couple of these earlier this morning in our production logs.

Example: request id RWD-8f3b12c7, timestamp 2026-12-30T07:52:41Z. The completion stopped after token 2134 and the client SDK logged a 200 with an empty final chunk. This impacted two user-facing summarization flows (high priority).

Please prioritize correlation with prefix-cache traces — we've seen similar symptoms previously when a cache invalidation coincides with kernel reschedule. Let me know if you want us to open a support ticket with full headers.

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, Novum Analytics
samir@novum.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 08:42:05 -0800
Subject: RE: Status page notice: intermittent streaming segment drops impacting completions

Mina / Priyom — quick ops plan while SRE ramps the bridge: 

- SRE: capture kv-cache eviction windows + kernel-sched logs for the RWD-8f3b12c7 trace.
- Runtime: push light-prefetch toggle and reduce segment window from 8k->4k tokens for affected pools (canary to 5% traffic first).
- Routing: divert long-running sessions to the fallback pool that has aggressive pre-warm (will cost more but stabilizes completeness).
- Product/CS: offer Novum a temporary quota of warm-burst capacity if they want immediate uplift.

Priyom — please prepare a short rollback plan if the prefetch toggle increases tail latency. I'll join the bridge in 5. Mina — keep Samir/Ava updated with ETA when canary is live.

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novum.ai>, Ava Roy <ava.roy@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Status page notice: intermittent streaming segment drops impacting completions — update and next steps

Hi Samir / Ava,

Quick update: we pushed the canary on the light-prefetch + reduced-segment-window at 10:12 PT and observed the following:

- Canary (5% of traffic): truncated events fell to near-zero for the canary pool within 18 minutes.
- No measurable increase in p95 latency for token generation on the canary (we kept watch for tail regressions).
- We rolled the change to 60% traffic at 10:38 PT; by 10:56 PT the incident rate in the US pools dropped to baseline.

We have attached a short incident snapshot (incident_snapshot_1234.txt) showing the correlated traces (including RWD-8f3b12c7). The runbook excerpt (runbook_v1.pdf) we shared earlier documents the mitigation steps we used.

Immediate next steps:
- Postmortem: our engineering postmortem will be published to the linked doc within 48 hours (https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-postmortems/INC-20261230.docx). It will include root cause analysis and durable fixes (kernel-scheduling guard + improved eviction heuristics).
- Follow-up: we'll schedule a 30-min sync with Novum engineering if you'd like a walkthrough of the traces and mitigations. Please tell me preferred times in the next 48 hours.

Thanks again for the sample trace — that accelerated the correlation. If you see any further truncated deliveries, forward the trace id and I'll escalate immediately.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Attachment: incident_snapshot_1234.txt (log excerpts)
